# Brik

> A tiny reactive runtime for interfaces that build themselves. One JavaScript file. No npm, no compiler, no virtual DOM.

Brik is for an agent that has to put a UI in the browser. It is not React, Vue, Next, or Astro. Do not add a router, a bundler, or another framework unless the user asks.

## Install

Runtime: https://brikjs.pages.dev/v1/brik.min.js

Theme, optional: https://brikjs.pages.dev/v1/brik-theme.min.css

Checksums: https://brikjs.pages.dev/v1/integrity.json

```html
<body>
  <brik app></brik>
  <script defer src="https://brikjs.pages.dev/v1/brik.min.js"></script>
</body>
```

## API

- `Brik.component(name, fn)` registers a component. The name matches `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/`.
- `Brik.mount(node?)` mounts `<brik>` elements and returns `unmount()`.
- `Brik.h(tag, props, ...children)` creates DOM. String children are text. Function children are reactive text. `html` and `unsafeHTML` are trusted markup.
- `Brik.state(value)` is a shallow Proxy. Replacing a property is reactive. Mutating a nested object in place is not.
- `Brik.effect(fn)` reruns when a value it read changes. It may return a cleanup. Effects created after `await` are not owned by the mount.

Nested `<brik name>` elements mount after the parent renders. HTML strings returned by a component are trusted. Untrusted text goes through `Brik.h()` as a child. Never evaluate JavaScript supplied by an agent or a network.

## Theme

`brik-theme` is a stylesheet of bricks on native elements. Set `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`. Button roles are `primary`, `secondary`, `tint`, and `ghost`. The CSS works without the runtime.
